edges.limitations: In mice Npt2a carries most proximal-tubule phosphate reabsorption, so Npt2c loss alone is compensated; in humans NPT2c loss is sufficient to cause phosphate wasting. The species difference in transporter dependence limits the single knockout as an HHRH model.

edges.description: Double knockout develops hypophosphatemic rickets rescued by dietary phosphate.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC34A3 variants remove or reduce NaPi-IIc sodium-phosphate cotransport at the proximal-tubule brush border. Alleles include truncating frameshifts such as the founder c.228delC, splice-site and intronic deletions causing aberrant splicing, and missense variants. Missense alleles act by different routes: some are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, while others reach the cell surface but are degraded faster or transport phosphate with reduced maximal velocity.

nodes.description: Combined loss of Npt2a and Npt2c reproduces severe hypophosphatemia, hypercalciuria and rickets, and a high-phosphate diet rescues phosphate and bone.
Mice lacking Npt2c alone do not waste phosphate on a normal-phosphate diet, unlike human HHRH.

Oral phosphate supplementation alone is standard care and typically normalizes serum phosphate. In the original kindred it reversed the clinical and biochemical abnormalities except the renal phosphate leak itself. In a pooled analysis it corrected hypophosphatemia in more than half of individuals but often did not resolve kidney or bone outcomes, and response depended on genotype and baseline TRP. Active vitamin D analogues are contraindicated, because calcitriol is already raised and they would worsen the hypercalciuria. Phosphate supplementation can raise PTH, and secondary hyperparathyroidism has developed on treatment, so PTH is monitored. Long-term data on preventing renal calcification are lacking.
